answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction model. Each new identity competes for limited resource allocation slots by proposing original work, which is graded by a panel of established peers, creating a kernel of trust. As more identities emerge, the cost to secure a slot rises significantly; for instance, a slot may start at $10 but can escalate to $100 or more with a dozen competing. This escalating cost traps attackers on a financial island, as maintaining fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive, akin to trying to create an oasis in a desert.
